## Email draft

**To:** submission@aiqtlab.com
**Subject:** Qiskit Fall Fest 2026 Warsaw · Track 2 submission · [TEAM NAME]

Hello,

Please find our Track 2 (Quantum machine learning) submission below.

- **Team:** [TEAM NAME]
- **Members:** Wyatt Reisz
- **Track:** 2, Quantum machine learning
- **Project:** Does a time crystal make a better quantum memory? A Floquet spin-chain reservoir vs classical forecasters on real data
- **Repository (public):** https://github.com/wdreisz/floquet-reservoir
- **Demo video:** [VIDEO LINK]
- **Slides:** `presentation/deck.pdf` in the repository (`deck.html` is the interactive version)

**Summary.** We use a 6-spin disordered kicked-Ising (Floquet) chain as a quantum reservoir computer and benchmark it against an echo-state network with the same 11 features, linear autoregression, persistence and a non-interacting control. We use yearly sunspots and Mauna Loa CO2, with identical time-ordered splits, validation-only tuning and 8 seeds. Time-crystal order hurts memory (capacity 1.32 vs 5.75 in the scrambling regime). Linear AR is the best forecaster on both series, and the classical models win. Rolling-origin cross-validation (4 folds) keeps the AR > ESN > quantum order on both series by mean rank. In those folds the quantum reservoir beats persistence on sunspots in median (0.26 vs 0.41) but is worse in 1 of 4 folds. We also show the shot-noise and restart cost of running it on hardware. All results are classical simulation; no quantum hardware was used and no quantum advantage is claimed.

The README has environment instructions, and one command regenerates every result (about 90 s on a laptop).

Best regards,
Wyatt Reisz

## Demo video shot list (about 2 minutes)

| Time | Shot | Say |
|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:12 | Deck slide 1 (title) | Time crystals are the most robust phase of a driven spin chain. Does that make them a better quantum memory? |
| 0:12–0:30 | Deck slide 3 (circuit) | Six spins; reset qubit 0 to encode the input; two Floquet kicks; read 11 expectation values; train only a ridge readout. Exact density-matrix simulation, checked against Qiskit Aer. |
| 0:30–0:45 | Deck slide 4 (method) | Same features, same splits, tuned on validation only, 8 seeds, Diebold–Mariano tests. ESN, AR, persistence and a no-interaction quantum control. |
| 0:45–1:05 | Deck slide 5 (memory figure); point at panel (a) and the time-crystal band | Scrambling kicks reach ESN-level memory; the time crystal forgets (1.32 vs 5.75). |
| 1:05–1:25 | Streamlit app (`streamlit run app/app.py`): move the θ slider from 0.5π to 0.95π | Live: memory profile collapses as we enter the time-crystal phase. |
| 1:25–1:45 | Deck slides 6–8 (forecasting, cross-validation, where classical wins) | Linear AR wins both series, ESN second, quantum third. On CO2 interactions clearly help; on sunspots it is about persistence. |
| 1:45–1:55 | Deck slide on measurement cost | With 1,000 shots the memory advantage mostly disappears, and every readout needs a restart. |
| 1:55–2:05 | Terminal: `python -m qreservoir.experiments`, then `pytest` passing; README on GitHub | Classical simulation only, no advantage claimed. Everything regenerates in about 90 seconds. Repo link on screen. |
